inline_comments.comment:
`role="status"` carries an implicit `aria-live="polite"`, so rendering it together with `aria-live="assertive"` sends contradictory signals to assistive technology. Screen readers that honour the role's implicit politeness may ignore the explicit attribute, or behave inconsistently.

Fix: derive the role from the politeness prop:
```tsx
role={politeness === 'assertive' ? 'alert' : 'status'}
```
`role="alert"` is the ARIA-specified equivalent for assertive live regions, and the WAI-ARIA spec lists it as carrying an implicit `aria-live="assertive"` — consistent with the explicit attribute value.

The JSDoc comment says "string for exact match" but the implementation uses `content.includes(text)`, which is a substring match. This mismatch can cause false positives: for example `{ text: 'pass' }` would match a region containing `'3 tests passed'`.

Either correct the implementation to use strict equality (`content === text`) for string inputs, or update the comment to say "substring match" so callers have accurate expectations.

`expect(el).toBeDefined()` passes for any non-`undefined` value, including stale detached nodes. For asserting a DOM element is present in the document, prefer jest-dom's `expect(el).toBeInTheDocument()`, which is consistent with the rest of this project's test suite and fails meaningfully when the element has been removed.

The description `'fails when no matching live region is found'` is ambiguous — it reads as though the test itself is expected to fail. A clearer name would be `'throws when no matching live region is found'` or `'rejects when text does not match any live region'`.
`args: {}` is redundant — omitting the `args` key entirely is equivalent and keeps the story object minimal. If no default args are needed for `PolitenessToggle`, remove the property.

`toHaveLiveRegion` and `LiveRegionMatcherOptions` are test-only utilities (custom Vitest/jest matchers) being re-exported from the production components barrel. Per the project's conventions, testing utilities should live under a `test-utils/` path rather than the main bundle entry so they are not shipped to end-user builds. Consider moving them behind a dedicated test-utils export (e.g. `storybook/internal/test-utils`) and removing them from this file.

general_comments.comment: The PR description lists three significant pieces of work that are entirely absent from the diff: (1) adding `extend-to-be-announced` as a devDependency and registering it in `code/.storybook/storybook.setup.ts`, (2) the `TestProviderRender` announcement integration (announce test-run lifecycle events), and (3) the three accompanying `AnnouncesTestRunStart` / `AnnouncesTestRunFinished` / `AnnouncesTestRunCrashed` stories. If these are coming in a follow-up PR the description is misleading; if they are required for the feature to be functional end-to-end, the PR is incomplete. The diff as shown only adds the base `LiveRegion` component, which is not wired into any live Storybook surface.

Two distinct announcement mechanisms are now exported side-by-side with no guidance on when to use each:
- **Declarative** `<LiveRegion>` renders an `aria-live` div inside the React tree; changes to `children` trigger announcements.
- **Imperative** `announce()` (re-exported from `@react-aria/live-announcer`) injects hidden live-region nodes directly into `document.body`.

Using both for the same event — e.g. updating a `<LiveRegion>` child AND calling `announce()` — will cause the message to be announced twice. The JSDoc on each export should explicitly guide consumers: prefer the declarative component when inside a React render; use the imperative function for side-effects outside the render cycle. Add a note warning against combining them for the same message.
